query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: Avg Subcategory Score
per_column.rationale: A composite mean of the existing numeric subcategory ratings (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment, Value For Money). It provides a single continuous severity axis that can be regressed against Recommended, so it has some analytical leverage, but it largely restates information already in the original numeric columns and correlates strongly with Overall Rating, limiting its novelty. Values are directly derivable from present columns; sample values track the sentiment of the shown text well (1.2 for the broken-seat rant, 5.0 for the 'can't get it any better' rave), so groundedness is high.

per_column.name: Value For Money Poor
per_column.rationale: A binary threshold flag over the existing Value For Money column. It is topically relevant to why a flight is not recommended, but as a bare yes/no restatement of an original numeric column it adds only modest leverage beyond the raw score. It is well grounded: row 1 (paid $2300, seat broke) correctly reads as poor value; row 5 marked 'no' is defensible since the complaint is about baggage handling/compensation rather than fare value, and the flag reflects the underlying numeric rating.

per_column.name: Overall Rating Band
per_column.rationale: A high/medium/low bucketing of the existing Overall Rating. Useful for grouping/segmenting non-recommended vs recommended reviews, but redundant with the original numeric rating. Grounding is sound where checkable: the broken-seat review bands 'low', the two rave reviews band 'high'. Note a mild internal tension with Non-Rec Risk Factors on row 5 (band 'medium' yet flagged 'very_low_overall_rating'), which slightly undercuts confidence but is isolated.

per_column.name: Weakest Category
per_column.rationale: Identifies the lowest-scoring service dimension per review, giving a genuinely new categorical axis to explain WHICH aspect drives non-recommendation — directly on point for the query. Grounding is generally good (row 1 'Seat Comfort' matches the broken-seat text; row 2 'Staff Service' matches the slow-service complaint; row 5 'Value For Money' matches the compensation grievance). It is lowered somewhat because on uniformly positive reviews the argmin still labels a 'weakest' category that the text contradicts (rows 3 and 4 label 'Seat Comfort' despite the seat being praised as outstanding), a tie-break artifact rather than an invented fact.

per_column.name: Non-Rec Risk Factors
per_column.rationale: The most query-aligned column: it enumerates the concrete driver(s) (poor food, poor seat, poor value, low overall, poor staff) behind a non-recommendation, offering a multi-label decomposition analysts can group and count on. Mostly grounded via thresholds on the underlying ratings and corroborated by text (row 1's multi-factor tag matches the seat/value/staff complaints). Groundedness is tempered by threshold-derived factors not always evidenced in the visible text (e.g. row 1's 'poor_food_beverages' is unmentioned) and the row-5 case flagging 'very_low_overall_rating' while Overall Rating Band reads 'medium', an inconsistency that suggests occasional over-assertion.

judge.rationale: The added columns are collectively well-aimed at the query. Weakest Category and Non-Rec Risk Factors provide real new analytical axes for diagnosing WHY a Business-Class flight is not recommended, while Avg Subcategory Score, Value For Money Poor, and Overall Rating Band are relevant but largely thresholded restatements of existing numeric columns, so their marginal leverage is lower. On groundedness, values are consistently derivable from the table's numeric rating fields and corroborate the sampled review text (negative reviews yield low composites/appropriate weakest categories; rave reviews yield high bands). The main caveats are tie-break artifacts (labelling a 'weakest' category on uniformly positive reviews) and a single cross-column inconsistency (medium band vs 'very_low_overall_rating' flag), which modestly reduce but do not undermine overall grounding. No outright fabricated facts were observed.
